To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have successfully corrected a urea cycle disorder in organoid derived hepatocytes.

1) we successfully reprogrammed fibroblasts from a patient with OTC into iPSCs; 2) we used CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing to correct the OTC mutation; 3) we differentiated the corrected iPSCs into hepatocyte-like cells and 4) we demonstrated that the edited cells had corrected the OTC mutation and were capable of synthesizing argininosuccinic acid, the first enzyme of the Urea Cycle.

we have successfully reprogrammed fibroblasts from a patient with OTC deficiency, corrected the genetic defect in these cells and then differentiated them into hepatic organoid like structures that have the ability to correct the urea cycle defect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of stem cell technology for the treatment of genetic liver diseases, and the use of gene editing to correct genetic defects in these diseases.
the development of a novel approach to cell based therapy for urea cycle defects.
the development of a novel approach to the treatment of urea cycle disorders, and the development of a model that can be used to study and potentially treat a broad range of liver diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach we describe here is applicable to other liver diseases, and could be used to identify successful strategies for cell based therapy.

the use of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing technology to correct a genetic defect in a urea cycle disease in patient derived hepatocyte like cells, is an effective approach for the development of cell based therapies.

we have successfully reprogrammed a somatic cell line derived from a patient with an inherited deficiency in the urea cycle into a pluripotent stem cell line and then differentiated these cells into hepatocyte like cells that express the urea cycle genes and proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this report describes the successful reprogramming, genetic correction and differentiation of somatic cells derived from a patient with urea cycle disease.
we have successfully reprogrammed somatic cells from patients with urea cycle disorders, and then genetically corrected them using a CRISPR-Cas9 system.

we have demonstrated a successful, and widely applicable approach, for the generation of patient-specific stem cells from a patient suffering from a urea cycle disorder, their genetic correction, and the differentiation of the edited cells into hepatic organoid like cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a novel and efficient approach to correct genetic defects in liver organoids derived from patient stem cells.

we have demonstrated that the genetic correction of a urea cycle disorder in a patient specific induced pluripotent stem cell derived hepatic cell line can be accomplished and that this can be used for the correction of the urea cycle defect in vitro.

it demonstrates the feasibility of the approach for genetic correction of liver cells and the generation of patient derived hepatocyte-like cells for use in the investigation of liver disease and the development of novel therapeutics.
